likelyQuestions: Calculate the number of comparisons made by a QuickSort partition algorithm using the first element as pivot for a strictly increasing array versus a strictly decreasing array of size n.
Solve the recurrence relation T(n) = T(n/3) + T(2n/3) + n using appropriate methods.
Write both recursive and non-recursive algorithms for calculating the nth Fibonacci number, analyze their time and space complexities, and compare their efficiencies.
Given a sorted array of distinct integers, design an algorithm to find if there exists an index i such that T[i] equals i in O(log n) time, and prove its worst-case complexity.
Formulate a greedy algorithm to maximize the number of programs stored on a disk of fixed capacity given varying program sizes, and analyze its time complexity.
Explain the partition mechanism of QuickSort with a suitable example and determine its best-case and worst-case time complexities.
Solve the recurrence relation T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n log n using the Master Theorem or substitution method.
Write an iterative algorithm to generate the Fibonacci series up to n terms, ensuring optimal space complexity O(1).
Design a modified binary search algorithm to find a fixed point in a sorted array where elements can be negative, and provide a formal complexity analysis.

Consider the optimal storage on tape or disk problem. Prove that sorting the program sizes in ascending order yields the maximum number of programs that can be stored within a capacity limit D, and state the greedy choice property.
